deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a fair-copy prose notebook entry, likely lecture or reading notes on ancient Greek history in the Göttingen style associated with Heeren. It is headed 'Geschichte von Sparta' and continues the previous page's notes on Greek national institutions (games, the Amphictyony). Its content, restated:

1. Geography. The Spartan territory is of moderate size, not very fertile and mountainous. It contains Mount Taygetus and the main river Eurotas. Its capital, Sparta, is called one of the largest but not the most beautiful of cities, echoing Thucydides I.10.

2. Pre-Dorian period. The land was once ruled by Achaeans: King Menelaus, then Orestes, then Tisamenus as the last.

3. Dorian migration. It falls in Tisamenus' time, dated c. 1080 BC. The Dorians expelled the Achaeans, and the constitution was changed so that the houses of Procles and Eurysthenes stayed in power (the Spartan dual kingship).

4. Rise of Sparta. Sparta became the capital and its citizens the ruling people. Some towns revolted, especially Helos, and were punished by being made serfs (the traditional etymology of 'helots').

5. Following centuries. Sparta was chiefly at war with the Argives. The sentence 'Die Verfassung wurde …' continues on folio 59 ('sehr zerrüttet…'), which leads to Lycurgus c. 880 BC.

There is no derivation, computation or mathematical problem on this page. The only numerical content is two traditional chronological dates: 1080 here and 880 on the next page.
errors: No mathematical errors, since there is no mathematics.

Historically, the date c. 1080 BC for the Dorian migration and c. 880 BC for Lycurgus are conventional dates from early-19th-century handbooks. They are not errors relative to the period's scholarship, but modern scholarship treats both the Dorian migration and Lycurgus as largely legendary.
The derivation of the helots from the town of Helos is the ancient folk etymology (Strabo, Ephorus) that the notes repeat. It is doubtful today but standard for the time.
